prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts an indoor retail or cafe space with glass-door refrigerators along the left wall (roughly 1 to 3 m away in frames 1–2), a central small round table with a brown paper bag and bottles on top, a seated woman in the foreground of frame 1 (~1 m away, facing right), a seated person in a beanie to the left of the table (~2.5 m away in frame 1, facing right and downward), a standing man in a red-and-black plaid shirt behind the table (~3 m away in frame 1, facing left toward the table and downward rather than at the camera wearer), and distant store shelves 5 to 8 m back on the right in frames 3–5. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer walks forward and pitches their view downward and slightly right toward the table, reducing the distance to the table and paper bag from ~2.5 m to ~0.5 m and to the standing man from ~3 m to ~1 m, while the foreground woman exits the bottom edge after frame 2 and the seated beanie wearer exits the lower-left edge after frame 4. By frames 4 and 5, the camera wearer's right hand holding a white slip of paper enters the bottom-right foreground at ~0.3 to 0.4 m (within arm's reach of the paper bag, which is also within the standing man's reach), while the standing man's head is cropped above the top frame edge and his lower legs are occluded behind the table and bag. Compared to the motion-blurred RGB strip, the depth map much more clearly separates the foreground silhouettes—such as the upright cylinder of the paper bag, the round tabletop plane, and the bottle profiles—from the cluttered background. However, the depth map is unreliable on reflective and transparent surfaces like the glass refrigerator doors and partition walls, merges the paper bag's depth into the standing man's torso in frame 3, and loses fine thin structures like table legs and distant shelf details.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities against a black background as the camera wearer approaches the central group (~2.5–3 m away in frame 1 down to ~0.5–1 m in frame 5), detecting the close seated woman in frame 1 (~1 m in front, facing right), the seated person in the beanie on the left (~2.5 m to ~1 m away across frames 1–4, spaced ~1 m left of the table and facing right), and the standing man on the right (~3 m to ~1 m away, facing left in frames 1–2 before turning his torso toward the camera wearer in frames 3–5 while his head leaves the upper frame). In frame 2, when the camera wearer is ~2 m from the grouping, the map specifically segments small objects within arm's reach of the two people at the table: the handheld device in the seated person's lap (labeled 'remote'), items on the tabletop below the bag (labeled 'book' and 'bottle'), and the tall brown paper bag on the right side of the table (labeled 'handbag'), before the camera wearer's own right arm enters from the lower right in frame 5 (labeled 'person' at ~0.3 m, within arm's reach of the bag). Unlike the RGB image where motion blur and dark clothing blend the seated people and tabletop items into the dark chairs and floor, the coloured masks sharply delineate overlapping person boundaries in frame 1 and highlight the small objects on and near the table in frame 2. However, the segmentation map is highly inconsistent across frames and frequently misclassifies or drops objects: it completely misses all people and objects in frame 1's table area except the three people, drops the paper bag and bottles in frames 3–5, leaves a hollow cutout inside the standing man's torso where the bag occludes him in frame 3, and mislabels the smartphone as a 'remote', the paper bag as a 'handbag', a glass partition edge on the left of frame 5 as a 'laptop', and the camera wearer's own forearm as a separate 'person'.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map tracks the joint positions and orientations of the people in the scene on a black background, showing the seated person on the left in frame 2 (~2 m away, facing right with arms bent forward holding an object in their lap) and the standing man on the right in frames 2 and 3 (~2 m and ~1.5 m away, standing ~1 m to the right of the seated person). In frame 2 the standing man's torso and facial keypoints are angled to the left toward the table and his right hand is raised near his face, whereas in frame 3 his shoulders rotate to face more directly toward the camera wearer while his head tilts down toward the table and his left arm hangs down within arm's reach of the paper bag. By frame 5, when the camera wearer is within ~1 m of the standing man (whose head is cropped out of the top of the frame and legs are occluded below the table), the map renders dense magenta hand skeletons for the standing man's left hand reaching down toward the bag (~0.7 m away) and the camera wearer's own right hand extending from the bottom-right corner (~0.3 m away, within arm's reach of both the bag and the man's hand) alongside a partial yellow arm skeleton. This skeletal representation makes exact limb articulation, shoulder turn, head pitch, and hand-to-hand proximity immediately legible despite the severe motion blur in frame 3 and the tight cropping in frame 5. Nonetheless, the pose map is unreliable across the sequence because it completely fails to detect any skeletons in the blurry first frame or the downward-angled fourth frame, misses the seated person on the left in frames 3–4, and hallucinates a distorted yellow lower-body leg structure attached to the camera wearer's outstretched right arm in frame 5.
